entities.summary:
Thomas of Frignano (born c. 1305, died November 27, 1381) emerged as a prominent Italian Franciscan theologian and ecclesiastical administrator during the tumultuous Great Schism of the Western Church. His career, spanning the mid-14th century, saw him rise through the ranks of the Order of Friars Minor, culminating in his appointment as Minister General, a position of immense influence within one of Europe's largest religious orders. His subsequent elevation to Patriarch of Grado by Pope Gregory XI positioned him at the heart of papal politics and the ongoing struggle for ecclesiastical authority in the Adriatic region, making him a significant figure in both Franciscan history and the broader religious landscape of late Medieval Italy.

Born in Frignano, near Modena, Thomas joined the Franciscan order early in life and distinguished himself as a scholar and preacher. He held various leadership roles within the order before being elected Minister General in 1367, a crucial period marked by internal reform efforts and external pressure from secular rulers. During his tenure, he worked to uphold the Franciscan rule and strengthen the order's intellectual and spiritual foundations across Europe. Pope Gregory XI recognized his administrative acumen and theological orthodoxy, appointing him Patriarch of Grado on July 19, 1372. This patriarchal see, though titular for much of its history, held significant symbolic weight and jurisdictional claims over Venice's ecclesiastical province.
